parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish gruby, from Old East Slavic грубъ (grubŭ), from Proto-Slavic *grǫbъ. Doublet of gręby and hruby. Compare Kashubian grëbi and Silesian hruby.

parole.significato: keep, donjon (main tower of a castle or fortress, located within the castle walls)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic стълбъ (stŭlbŭ), from Proto-Slavic *stъlbъ (“post”). Doublet of słup, an inherited form.

parole.significato: dart (pointed missile weapon, intended to be thrown by the hand; for example, a short lance or javelin)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Polish sulica, possibly from Old East Slavic сулица (sulica), from Proto-Slavic *sudlica.

parole.significato: Vlach (person from Wallachia or of Wallachian descent)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic волохъ (voloxŭ), from Proto-Slavic *volxъ, from Proto-Germanic *walhaz. Doublet of Walia, wałach, Wałach, Włoch, and Włochy.

parole.significato: Vlach (person from Wallachia or of Wallachian descent)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old East Slavic, from Proto-Slavic *volšьskъ. By surface analysis, Wołoch + -ski. Doublet of włoski (“Italian”).
